findings.title: Unauthenticated GUI exposes destructive filesystem operations
findings.description: All API routes are unauthenticated and can create, restore, rename, delete backups, change config, start watchers, and terminate the process. The CLI allows binding the Flask app to an arbitrary host, so using --host 0.0.0.0 exposes local save-management primitives to the LAN. Even on localhost, routes with no JSON requirement such as /api/shutdown and /api/watcher/toggle are vulnerable to cross-site form-triggered CSRF.
findings.suggestion: Require an unguessable session token for every mutating route, generate it at startup, embed it in the page, and validate it server-side. Keep localhost as the default and require an explicit warning/confirmation for non-loopback binds. Consider rejecting remote addresses unless configured.

findings.title: Diagnostics leak local environment and paths
findings.description: /health returns Python version, executable path, platform, save paths, backup paths, save names, and directory listings without authentication. If the GUI is exposed beyond localhost, this leaks sensitive local filesystem layout and game metadata. This also makes A1 worse by giving attackers the exact target names needed for destructive API calls.
findings.suggestion: Gate diagnostics behind the same auth token as the API, or restrict /health to loopback-only. Redact executable paths and directory listings unless a debug mode is explicitly enabled.

findings.title: Rename flow is not transactional across saves and backups
findings.description: api_rename_save/preflight_rename/rename_save/rename_backups_for_save model a save rename as multiple independent filesystem operations. If rename_save succeeds but rename_backups_for_save fails due to permissions, cross-device behavior, a concurrent creator, or an unexpected destination state, the live save has the new name while backup history remains under the old name. That breaks the invariant that backup history follows the save.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a single service-level rename operation that owns both live-save and backup moves, performs all preflights immediately before mutation, and rolls back the live save rename if backup migration fails. Return one domain result from that service and have CLI/GUI call it instead of sequencing primitives.

findings.title: WatcherManager shared state is not thread-safe
findings.description: WatcherManager mutates _observer, _watchers, _watches, and _running without a manager-level lock. Flask request threads can call start/stop/watch/unwatch/pause_for concurrently, while watchdog/timer callbacks are also active. Interleavings can schedule on a stopped observer, unschedule a handle while stop is joining, lose watcher entries, or observe stale running state.
findings.suggestion: Add a reentrant lock around all WatcherManager methods that read or mutate observer/watch state. Keep SaveWatcher locks separate. Avoid exposing _watchers directly and make pause_for resolve the watcher under the manager lock.

findings.title: Config writes can lose updates under concurrent requests
findings.description: set_ performs load-modify-save with no file lock, and api_config writes each incoming key through separate set_ calls. Two concurrent requests can both load the same old config and overwrite each other's changes. A multi-key update can also be partially visible because each key is persisted independently.
findings.suggestion: Serialize config access with a process-level lock and, if multiple processes are possible, an OS file lock. Replace per-key writes in api_config with a single validate-then-save update that writes the entire config atomically once.

findings.title: Auto-backup performs long filesystem copy while holding watcher lock
findings.description: SaveWatcher._do_backup holds self._lock while calling create_backup, which can recursively copy thousands of save files and prune backups. During that time pause(), cancel_pending(), resume(), and new file events block. A restore or stop request can therefore wait behind a long backup, defeating the pause invariant and making shutdown/unwatch unresponsive.
findings.suggestion: Under the lock, decide whether a backup is needed and mark a backup-in-progress state, then release the lock before create_backup. Reacquire the lock only to update last-backup metadata. Use the in-progress state to prevent duplicate concurrent backups.

findings.title: Backup creation publishes an empty backup directory before content is complete
findings.description: _unique_destination creates the final destination directory before copy starts, then create_backup copies into a sibling temp directory and moves files into the already-visible destination one by one. list_backups treats any directory as a valid backup, so another request or GUI refresh can see and restore/delete an incomplete backup while it is still being populated.
findings.suggestion: Keep in-progress backups outside the visible namespace or mark them explicitly as incomplete. Copy into a temp directory, then atomically rename the completed directory to the final timestamp path. Reserve names with a lock file or mkdir on a hidden reservation path rather than exposing the final directory early.

findings.title: Pruning disabled for max_count zero despite API wording
findings.description: prune_auto_backups returns immediately when max_count <= 0, so a configured max_auto_backups value of 0 keeps all automatic backups. The docstring says it deletes old backups so at most max_count remain, and create_backup calls it for max_auto >= 0. This is an invariant mismatch that can cause unbounded disk growth.
findings.suggestion: Define one explicit semantic. If 0 means keep none, remove the early return and prune all autos. If 0 means disable pruning, rename the setting or document it consistently in the config UI and function docstring.

overall_assessment: The core domain is small and understandable, but destructive filesystem operations, watcher orchestration, and config persistence are exposed through thin GUI/CLI wrappers without a strong service boundary. The largest risks are unauthenticated local web control, non-transactional multi-step filesystem mutations, and unprotected shared state in the watcher/config subsystems.
summary: 7 majors, 1 minor — security boundary and concurrency invariants need rework before approval
